item.title: Enoshima Aquarium Guide: Tickets, Highlights & Access
item.description: Right on the Shonan coast facing Enoshima island, the Enoshima Aquarium — affectionately known as “Enosui” — is one of the Tokyo area’s most beloved aquariums, blending marine science with a stunning seaside setting. Its star exhibits showcase Sagami Bay, the deep, biodiverse waters just offshore, in a giant tank teeming with sardines, plus a dreamy jellyfish hall, playful dolphin and sea-lion shows staged against a backdrop of the real ocean and Mt.

item.title: Enoshima Guide: Shrine, Sea Candle & Sunset (Kanagawa)
item.description: A small sacred island linked to the Shonan coast by a bridge, Enoshima is one of the most beloved escapes near Tokyo — a hill of shrines, caves, gardens and sea views topped by a lighthouse-like observation tower. Climb (or ride the outdoor escalators) past the Enoshima Shrine to the Sea Candle, whose deck delivers superb panoramas over Sagami Bay to Mt. Fuji, gorgeous at sunset. Below, the wave-carved Iwaya caves and a lively lane of seafood and grilled-octopus stalls make it a perfect half-day, easily paired with the Shonan beaches.

item.title: Shonan Coast Guide: Beaches, Enoden & Access
item.description: The Shonan coast is the Tokyo area’s beloved beach playground — a sunny, laid-back stretch of sand and surf running from Kamakura past Enoshima toward Hiratsuka, all under the gaze of Mt. Fuji on clear days. This is where city-dwellers come to swim, surf, cycle and watch the sunset, riding the charming retro Enoden train as it rattles between the sea and old neighbourhoods. With beaches, Enoshima island, fresh shirasu, and an easygoing California-meets-Japan vibe, Shonan is the perfect seaside complement to historic Kamakura.

item.title: Shonan Shirasu Guide: Whitebait Bowls & Where to Eat
item.description: Along Kanagawa’s Shonan coast, the local delicacy is shirasu — tiny, translucent whitebait (baby sardines and anchovies) landed fresh from Sagami Bay. Served gleaming and raw (nama-shirasu) when the boats are out, or gently boiled (kama-age) and piled over rice, it’s the signature taste of a day at Enoshima and the Shonan beaches. A shirasu-don — a bowl of rice heaped with whitebait, perhaps with an egg yolk and ginger — is the dish to seek out, best enjoyed at a seaside diner with the surf in view.

item.title: Shonan Surfing Guide: Beaches, Lessons & Access
item.description: The Shonan coast is the birthplace and beating heart of Japanese surf culture — a sunny stretch of Sagami Bay where Tokyoites have been riding waves for generations. With gentle beach breaks, a string of surf shops and schools, and Mt. Fuji on the horizon, it’s the most accessible place near the capital to learn to surf or paddle out. Beginners can take a lesson and rent a board on the same beach where locals trade waves at dawn, while the laid-back seaside towns of Kugenuma, Katase and Chigasaki keep the whole scene relaxed and welcoming.

item.title: Kanagawa Nature Guide: Hakone Volcanoes, Kamakura Trails & Shonan Coast
item.description: Kanagawa contains more ecological variety than any other prefecture near Tokyo. Within 90 minutes of Shinjuku you can stand inside an active volcanic crater, hike a mountain ridge used by samurai armies, surf a Pacific beach, or kayak among sea caves on a wild volcanic cape. The prefecture is almost entirely overlooked by nature travellers who default to the Japanese Alps — a significant mistake.
